documents.title: Gallbladder again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good morning. Just letting you know I had another gallbladder attack Saturday night after we went out to dinner (I had the fish and chips, I know). Same pain under my right ribs going around to my back, lasted about 3 hours and then went away on its own. No fever and my eyes weren't yellow. I'm fine now and ate normally yesterday. Should I be doing anything?

documents.title: RE: Gallbladder again
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Sandra, thanks for letting me know, and glad it settled. That sounds like the same biliary colic you've had before. Since these keep coming back, I'd still recommend seeing a general surgeon about taking the gallbladder out - I'm happy to put in the referral whenever you say the word. If pain goes longer than 4-5 hours, or you get fever, chills, yellow skin or eyes, or dark urine, go to the ED rather than waiting it out. We can talk more at your visit next week.

documents.title: RE: RE: Gallbladder again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you. I really can't be out for surgery before the school year is over. Can I call you in June about the referral?

Exam: NAD. Sclerae anicteric. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender in RUQ today, no mass. No edema.

ANNUAL PREVENTIVE VISIT

55F. Back at work since late August. Feels well. Last biliary attack in April, none since. Diabetes routine unchanged; no hypoglycemia; eye exam due in November. No chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations, edema. Bowels regular, no blood. No urinary complaints. Sleeping fine. Postmenopausal, no bleeding.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, glipizide 5 daily, lisinopril 10 daily, atorvastatin 20 qHS. NKDA.
Social: former smoker (quit 2015). Wine on weekends, 1-2 glasses. Walks most evenings in good weather.

PHQ-9: 2.

Exam: well appearing. Vitals as charted.
HEENT: TMs clear, oropharynx normal. Neck: no nodes, thyroid normal.
Breasts: deferred to mammogram per pt preference.
Heart RRR, no murmurs. Lungs clear.
Abd: obese, soft, nontender, no hepatosplenomegaly.
Ext: no edema. Feet: intact skin, normal monofilament, pulses 2+.
Skin: no suspicious lesions. Neuro: nonfocal.

A/P
1. Health maintenance: flu and COVID vaccines today. Mammogram ordered. Colonoscopy 2021 normal, next 2031. Pap/HPV 2022 negative, next due 2027. Shingrix and PCV20 complete. Tdap 2019. Hep C/HIV screened 2024.
2. T2DM: A1c, CMP, urine microalbumin today. Eye exam with optometry in Nov.
3. HTN: at goal. Continue lisinopril.
4. Lipids: on atorvastatin 20, fasting lipids today.
5. Cholelithiasis: quiet since April. She'll call if attacks return; referral offer stands.
6. Obesity: weight about stable. Encouraged continuing evening walks.

RTC 3-4 months.

events.reason: Right upper quadrant pain, fever and jaundice

results.text: No growth at 5 days (2 of 2 sets)

reports.text:
RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT ULTRASOUND (EMERGENCY)
Indication: RUQ pain, fever, jaundice.
Comparison: none available.
Findings: The common bile duct is dilated, with an echogenic shadowing stone lodged in its distal portion. The gallbladder contains multiple shadowing stones; no gallbladder wall thickening or pericholecystic fluid. Liver normal in echotexture without focal lesion. Visualized pancreas unremarkable. Right kidney without hydronephrosis. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Choledocholithiasis with common bile duct dilation; stone at the distal duct. Cholelithiasis.

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 12/01/2025

CC: Right-sided abdominal pain, fever, yellow eyes.

HPI: 55-year-old woman with known gallstones, type 2 diabetes and hypertension. Two days of constant pain under the right ribs, worse than her usual attacks and not letting up. Fevers and chills since yesterday. Noticed her eyes looked yellow this morning. Slow to answer and unsure of the date; history partly limited by her confusion.

PMH: T2DM, HTN, obesity, cholelithiasis with prior biliary colic.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, glipizide 5 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg qHS.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: Temp 38.9 C (102 F), BP 90/60, HR 110. Ill appearing, scleral icterus, disoriented to date. Abdomen: RUQ tenderness, no rebound, no guarding. Lungs clear. No rash.

Labs: WBC 18.0, Hgb 12.5, plt 250. Na 136, Cl 100, HCO3 16, anion gap 20, BUN 18, Cr 1.0. T bili 3.0 / direct 2.5, AST 80, ALT 75, alk phos 300. Lactate 4.5. Blood cultures x2 sent.
Bedside and formal RUQ US: dilated CBD with a distal stone; gallstones.

ED course: IV crystalloid bolus, with blood pressure and mentation improving. IV piperacillin-tazobactam after cultures. GI paged for ERCP.

Impression: acute cholangitis from choledocholithiasis.
Disposition: admitted to hospital medicine.

documents.title: ERCP Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
ENDOSCOPIC RETROGRADE CHOLANGIOPANCREATOGRAPHY
Date of procedure: 12/02/2025
Indication: acute cholangitis, distal CBD stone on ultrasound.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care.

The duodenoscope was passed to the second portion of the duodenum. The major papilla appeared normal. Deep biliary cannulation achieved. Cholangiogram showed a dilated common bile duct with a filling defect in the distal duct. Biliary sphincterotomy was performed. The stone was extracted with balloon sweeps, followed by purulent bile. Final occlusion cholangiogram showed no remaining filling defects. The pancreatic duct was not injected.

Impression: choledocholithiasis, cleared after sphincterotomy and balloon extraction.
Recommendations: continue antibiotics; general surgery referral for cholecystectomy in the coming weeks.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 12/01/2025, discharged 12/05/2025.

Diagnosis: acute cholangitis due to choledocholithiasis. Cholelithiasis.

Course: Presented with RUQ pain, fever, jaundice and confusion; hypotension and lactate 4.5 corrected with IV fluids in the ED and she did not need pressors or ICU care. Started on IV piperacillin-tazobactam. ERCP 12/02 with sphincterotomy and stone extraction, duct clear. Fever resolved by hospital day 2, confusion cleared within the first day, and bilirubin and liver enzymes trended down daily. Blood cultures no growth. Metformin and glipizide held while inpatient with correctional insulin; restarted on discharge with normal kidney function and good intake.

Discharge meds: amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg BID through 12/08 (7 days total antibiotics). Resume metformin 1000 mg BID, glipizide 5 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily (blood pressure normal by discharge), atorvastatin 20 mg qHS.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week with liver tests and CBC. General surgery clinic for interval cholecystectomy - appointment made for 12/22. Return for fever, pain or yellowing.

documents.title: Transition of Care Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt 2 business days after discharge (hospital records received 12/8). Feels "wiped out but so much better." No fever since the hospital. Pain gone. Eyes back to white. Eating small low-fat meals. Finished the last antibiotic dose last night. Back on all home meds as listed in the summary; fasting sugars a bit up the first day home, now back to her usual. Surgery appointment 12/22. Booked TCM visit with PCP 12/11 with labs. Knows to go to the ED for fever, pain or jaundice.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital follow-up. Discharge summary, ED record and ERCP report reviewed.

Admitted 12/1-12/5 with acute cholangitis from a distal common duct stone; ERCP 12/2 with sphincterotomy and clearance. Fluids and IV antibiotics, never needed the ICU. Finished amoxicillin-clavulanate 12/8.

Today: energy coming back, back at work half days this week. No pain, fever, chills. Stools and urine normal color. Eating low-fat. Sugars back to usual. Remembers little of the first evening in the ED.

Meds reconciled: metformin 1000 BID, glipizide 5, lisinopril 10, atorvastatin 20. Antibiotic course complete.

Exam: looks well. Afebrile. Sclerae anicteric. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, mild residual RUQ discomfort on deep palpation only, no guarding. No edema.

A/P
1. Choledocholithiasis with cholangitis - treated, duct cleared, clinically resolved. Liver tests and CBC today to confirm the trend.
2. Cholelithiasis - gallbladder still in with stones; she is now very motivated. Surgery consult 12/22 for interval cholecystectomy. Will need preop eval - book once surgery date is set.
3. T2DM/HTN - back on usual regimen, BP fine today.
Call or go to ED for fever, pain or jaundice before surgery.

documents.title: Follow-up labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sandra - your liver tests have come back to normal and your white count is normal too. That fits with the duct being fully cleared. Keep the 12/22 surgery appointment.

documents.title: General Surgery Consultation
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
GENERAL SURGERY CLINIC - CONSULTATION LETTER
Date of visit: 12/22/2025
Re: Sandra Wojcik, DOB 07/20/1970

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for asking us to see Ms. Wojcik after her admission earlier this month for acute cholangitis due to choledocholithiasis, treated with ERCP, sphincterotomy and stone extraction on 12/2. She has had gallstones on imaging since 2023 with intermittent biliary colic, and her mother and sister both had gallbladder disease.

She is pain free today and has completed antibiotics. Medical history: type 2 diabetes, hypertension, obesity. Prior C-section and tonsillectomy. Medications: metformin, glipizide, lisinopril, atorvastatin. NKDA. Former smoker.

Exam: well appearing. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed low transverse incision.

Assessment: symptomatic cholelithiasis after choledocholithiasis with cholangitis. Interval laparoscopic cholecystectomy is recommended to prevent recurrence. We discussed risks including bleeding, infection, bile leak, bile duct injury, conversion to open and the small chance of a further duct stone.

Plan: laparoscopic cholecystectomy scheduled 02/06/2026. Please complete a preoperative evaluation including a 12-lead ECG given her diabetes and hypertension, and send it to our office. Hold metformin, glipizide and lisinopril the morning of surgery.

Sincerely,
General Surgery
